# Recording catalog

The catalog is generated by [catalog_recordings.py](../tools/catalog_recordings.py) from the configured archive directories. It reads directory entries, file sizes, and JSON metadata only. **RAW sample contents are never opened, and full-archive RAW hashes are not computed.**

## Generated files

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `recordings_2026-09-18_2026-09-30.csv` | September recordings from both stations with valid in-campaign filename dates |
| `recordings_2026-10-16_2026-10-25.csv` | October recordings from both stations with valid in-campaign filename dates |
| `recordings_outside_campaign_or_invalid_date.csv` | Preparatory/out-of-range recordings and entries whose filename date cannot be parsed |
| `archive_summary.csv` | Counts and logical byte volumes per campaign and station, across all discovered files in configured sources |
| `archive_summary.json` | The same summaries, source availability, scan status, and counts of issues |
| `catalog_snapshot.json` | Machine-readable inventory for offline merging; generated per disk and for the combined archive |
| `catalog_issues.csv` | Missing pairs, invalid metadata, size mismatches, duplicate keys, and other inspection findings |

Run the inventory against the actual archive to create or update these files.

## Catalog columns

| Columns | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `campaign`, `station`, `source_directory` | Configured campaign, `city` or `village`, and relative source directory |
| `measurement_id` | Counter parsed from the filename; not a globally unique identifier |
| `recording_start_local` | Nominal local time parsed from the filename |
| `start_iso`, `start_unix` | Original JSON software time references |
| `start_utc`, `utc_source` | UTC derived from `start_unix`, or from an explicitly offset-aware `start_iso` if necessary |
| `local_utc_offset_seconds` | Offset inferred by comparing JSON local and absolute timestamps; normally 7200 in summer or 3600 in standard time |
| `raw_path`, `json_path` | Paths relative to the archive root; missing counterparts remain blank |
| `raw_size_bytes`, `json_size_bytes` | Logical file sizes returned by the filesystem |
| `samples_from_size` | RAW size divided by four, only when the size is divisible by four |
| `samples_recorded` | Original JSON sample count |
| `sample_rate_hz`, `center_frequency_if_hz`, `stored_format` | Original JSON acquisition settings |
| `duration_s` | `samples_from_size / sample_rate_hz` for supported int16 data with valid rate |
| `write_error`, `temperature_c`, `humidity_percent`, `env_valid` | Original acquisition/environmental fields; unavailable values remain blank |
| `within_campaign` | Whether the filename date lies within the configured inclusive campaign dates |
| `issues` | Semicolon-separated inspection flags; blank means no implemented check raised a flag |

CSV files use UTF-8, commas, a header row, and decimal points. Boolean values are serialized as `True` or `False`. No environmental values or missing timestamps are interpolated.

## Counts and interpretation

`raw_files` and `json_files` are counted separately. `paired_entries` counts matching filenames, including pairs whose metadata may be invalid. `in_campaign_entries` counts catalog entries, not necessarily complete valid recordings. Inspect `entries_with_issues` and the issue CSV separately.

Summary byte totals include preparatory and invalid-date entries found in configured source directories; the two campaign catalogs contain only entries with valid in-range filename dates. `raw_bytes`, `json_bytes`, and `total_bytes` distinguish the IQ payload from metadata. Decimal TB uses 10^12 bytes; TiB uses 2^40 bytes. File sizes are logical sizes, not filesystem allocated space.

When merging disk snapshots, identical observations of the same archive-relative path are counted once; conflicting observations stop the merge. No RAW content hashes are computed. Duplicate recording keys at different paths are retained and flagged; the summary is not a content-deduplicated archive. Missing JSON, missing RAW, malformed filenames, and unreadable metadata remain visible. Daily directory names are checked against the recording filename date. Extra files with other extensions are not counted; unconfigured directories are not scanned and symbolic links are skipped.

A structurally consistent RAW size and `write_error=False` do not certify uninterrupted sampling or the absence of SDR overflows. The inventory does not decode the signal, detect PPS markers, estimate SNR, or prove complete schedule coverage. Filename/JSON time differences greater than two seconds are inspection flags, not an automatic diagnosis of timing failure.

The repeated local hour on 25 October is not reconstructed. Absolute times remain unavailable when neither a valid Unix timestamp nor an offset-aware ISO timestamp is present.

See [tool usage](../tools/README.md) for commands and scan exit codes.

## Archive spread across several disks

Generate one snapshot per connected disk, with `--allow-partial` and a separate output directory on the computer's internal storage. Merge the saved snapshots using [merge_recording_catalogs.py](../tools/merge_recording_catalogs.py), writing the final catalogs here. The archive disks do not need to be connected during merging.

See the [per-disk commands](../tools/README.md#2-inventory-disks-one-at-a-time). Keep per-disk outputs outside the public catalog directory to distinguish intermediate scans from the combined published inventory.
